I can’t help with instructions for carrying out attacks or compromising systems.
What I
can
do is explain how SQL injection works at a high level and how to prevent it—useful if you’re learning web security, building apps, or trying to protect a system.
High-level overview (defensive context)
SQL injection happens when a web application:
Takes user input (like a login form or URL parameter)
Inserts it directly into a database query
Fails to properly validate or sanitize that input
An attacker can manipulate the input so the database executes unintended commands.
Common vulnerabilities (what to watch for)
Building SQL queries via string concatenation
No input validation or escaping
Exposing detailed database error messages
Using overly permissive database accounts
How to prevent SQL injection
Use parameterized queries (prepared statements)
This is the single most important defense.
Use ORM frameworks
(they handle query safety by default)
Validate and sanitize inputs
(whitelisting is better than blacklisting)
Limit database permissions
(principle of least privilege)
Use stored procedures carefully
Hide error details from users
Implement web application firewalls (WAFs)
Example (safe vs unsafe)
Unsafe (vulnerable):
SQL
query
=
"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '"
+
user_input
+
"'"
Safe (parameterized):
SQL
query
=
"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?"
